terms.grammar: conjunction, with the moods of sī
evidence: Cic. Sen. 21: crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
Cic. Tusc. 4.78: quō tē modō, inquit, accēpissem, nisi īrātus essem!
terms.comment: Negates the whole condition: “unless”. Where one word is negated, Latin says sī nōn (see if not). After a negative, nisi is “except, but”: nihil nisi, nothing but; nisi quod, except that.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the moods of sī
evidence: Catull. 14.1: nī tē plūs oculīs meīs amārem
terms.comment: The older form, frequent in comedy and poetry (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
phrases.english: but memory fades. — I dare say, unless you exercise it

phrases.latin: quō tē modō, inquit, accēpissem, nisi īrātus essem!
phrases.english: “how I would have dealt with you,” he said, “if I were not angry!”

phrases.latin: nī tē plūs oculīs meīs amārem
phrases.english: if I didn’t love you more than my own eyes

phrases.latin: nihil, nisi quod merīdiānus somnus eximitur
phrases.english: nothing (is different), except that the midday nap is dropped

phrases.latin: nūlla jam ultrā gēns, nihil nisi flūctūs et saxa
phrases.english: no people any more beyond us, nothing but waves and rocks
